label: PF Backlog 576
title: Eventing SSOT: ADR + design (Go-first bus, Python thin client, no-duplication, migration)
body:
## Problem / why
The Go-first + Python-thin-client decision, the no-duplication rule, single-writer ownership of the event
store, and the five open forks (Go packaging, daemon vs library, who serves SSE, store-writer ownership,
Python-emit handoff) are not yet recorded; coding cannot start unrecorded (AGENTS.md reconciliation).

## Goal / value
An accepted ADR + design doc with RECONCILIATION + IMPACT REVIEW so the capability is governed before build.

## In scope
- ADR (docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) recording Go-core + Python-thin-client, no second bus/store.
- Design doc with the consumer migration matrix + no-regression DoD + the five open decisions.

## Out of scope
- Any implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
- ADR accepted; design doc lists frozen contracts, migration matrix, and resolved open decisions.
- language/ownership conflicts recorded (events.jsonl owner; event_bus facade).

## Verification / test plan
- `python scripts/dev/design_review_check.py docs/<design>.md` clean; ADR index updated.

decisions.decision: Go event core + Python thin client over the A1 seam; strangle consumers behind shims
Extend go/pfcore first (Q1); standalone Go bus daemon (Q2); SSE at API edge (Q3)
Python stays the event-store writer until a one-time Go cutover (Q4); emit via the seam (Q5)

decisions.note: HIL approved Gate 1 for ADR-0011 PostgreSQL event authority design after design/spec/conformance pass.
Gate 1 re-recorded after reconciling Q4 writer ownership to ADR-0011.

evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=886051fa010e
BLOCKER:
  - AC-2 not evidenced: design pack records "Go core writes events/outbox" but no explicit `events.jsonl` owner and no `event_bus` facade ownership entry in `contracts`/`invariants`.
  - AC-1 partially unmet: `open_questions: []` yet in_scope cites "the five open decisions"; no resolved-decision list with dispositions appears in affected files.
MAJOR:
  - CL-008 guardrails unanswered in design: backup/restore path, scheduler/DB-down availability + startup check/lead-time, dry-run bounds, and fail-able test definition are absent.
  - Runtime role authorization gap: RLS stated, but no statement that runtime roles are subject to RLS (no BYPASSRLS/superuser inheritance) per guardrail 3.
  - Migration matrix not traceable: `spec_pack.migration_backfill` cites design sections 9/10, but no consumer-by-consumer migration matrix is enumerated in the declared artifacts.
  - Object-store orphan risk: FR-2 puts object before event commit; no stated cleanup/GC if the DB commit fails after successful put.
MINOR:
  - `risks: ['Not specified.']` — risks for a cross-cutting event-authority migration are undeclared.
  - Rollback for this item is only "Revert the change"; migration-interrupted recovery and JSONL projection parity criteria are unspecified (guardrail 6).
  - Observability lists metric names but no thresholds/SLO or alert lead-time for outbox lag/DLQ depth (guardrail 2/10).
  - Ownership gate (CL-001) dependency noted as "pending"; no recorded single-writer registration evidence for the facade seam.
NIT:
  - Rollback wording differs between `functional_spec.rollback` and `design_pack.rollback`; align to one canonical phrasing.
  - Three parallel spec/design artifacts (design + spec + spec-pack) risk drift; designate one SSOT and reference the rest.
SUMMARY:
  - Verdict: not gate-ready; both acceptance criteria lack verifiable evidence in declared artifacts.
  - Top risks: missing ownership/facade records (AC-2), unresolved "five open decisions" (AC-1), and guardrail checklist (CL-008) items unanswered before Gate 1.5.
  - Re-review after design doc explicitly records owners, resolved decisions, migration matrix rows, and guardrail answers.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=fa50497939a7
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - `spec_pack.config_contract` is N/A ("no config file change") yet `functional_spec.config_contract` defines EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT/EVENT_RETENTION with required startup validation and `contracts.files` lists `config/store-registry.json`; delta rows contradict within the same change.
MINOR:
  - Risk "Retention deletion removes referenced payload" is declared but has no matching failure-matrix/lifecycle control (e.g., delete object only when no live event row references it); "deletion via store contract" is not verifiable.
  - `traceability.test` for FR-1/2/3 is only "design review", omitting the BI-PF-1268/1269 tests named in FR `verification`; FR-2/FR-3 evidence omits `docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` despite design ref citing ADR-0011.
  - `api_contract` marked N/A while `migration_matrix` retargets `api/routers/events.py` to cursor reads; confirm no request/response contract delta or mark CONDITIONAL with evidence.
  - Outbox-lag/DLQ SLOs are asserted while Q2 defers the dispatcher daemon; add a rollout/enablement note so thresholds do not page before the dispatcher item lands.
  - Prior CL-001 minor: single-writer ownership is now stated in `invariants`, but no registration evidence artifact (registry/config entry) is named for the facade seam; record where registration will be evidenced.
NIT:
  - `contracts.files` lists `core/events.py`, `core/event_bus.py`, `config/store-registry.json` which are absent from `affected_files`; label the list as future contract surface vs. files changed by this design-only item to avoid impact-review confusion.
SUMMARY:
  - Delta resolves the prior blockers (ownership/AC-2, resolved Q1-Q5/AC-1) and most guardrails (CL-008, BYPASSRLS, migration matrix, orphan GC, risks, rollback, SSOT).
  - Verdict: approvable once the config-contract contradiction is reconciled; remaining items are evidence/traceability hardening.
  - Top residual risks: config-contract row mismatch, retention/reference integrity control, and SLO enablement sequencing ahead of the dispatcher.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=9ef3301bc1e6
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Rollback says "restore the projection" but gives no regeneration source or freshness bound after the Go writer stops; invariant 8 bars Python from writing authority, so if PostgreSQL is unavailable (the fail-closed trigger) events.jsonl cannot be rebuilt and the read path reverts to stale data — reversibility guardrail (CL-008 item 1) not fully answered.
  - `design_pack.contracts.files` is now empty while AC-1 requires frozen contracts; the file-level surface was moved to `contract_surface_future` (labelled future), leaving no frozen file contract for the facade/projection seam at Gate 1.
MINOR:
  - `design_pack.version` stays `1` despite substantive additions (failure_matrix rows, ownership_registration, decisions, contract_surface_future); approval audit cannot distinguish which version was accepted.
  - `config/store-registry.json` is declared in `design_pack.dependencies` but its registration entries only land in BI-PF-1268/1269; mark it a deferred dependency so Gate 1.5 does not assume evidence that does not yet exist.
  - Rollback ambiguity compounds the still-PENDING prior MAJOR disposition (CL-006: approval invalid while any MAJOR is PENDING).
NIT:
  - `spec_pack` and `functional_spec` are listed in `changed_fields` but their delta content is byte-identical to context (`functional_sha` unchanged) — scope noise for reviewers.
  - Guardrail 4 bound ("dry-run bounded to 1000 events") covers event rows only; the retention/object-GC path (`EVENT_PAYLOAD_STILL_REFERENCED`) has no explicit delete bound or dry-run mode.
SUMMARY:
  - Delta resolves most prior findings: retention control added to failure_matrix, config_contract now APPLICABLE, traceability includes BI-PF-1268/1269 tests, SLO enablement and ownership registration notes added, contracts.files separated into future surface.
  - No blockers; AC-1/AC-2 evidence (ADR, migration matrix, resolved Q1-Q5, ownership rows) is present.
  - Top risks: rollback projection-restore mechanism underspecified against the no-Python-writer invariant, and unresolved prior MAJOR dispositions must be closed before CL-006-valid Gate 1 approval.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=5e81d481897a
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Outbox rows committed from BI-PF-1268 have no dispatcher until BI-PF-1269, yet decisions declare lag/DLQ alerts inactive in that window and no interim backlog bound, cleanup, or lead-time alert is defined — unbounded, unobservable growth contradicts the "DB rows remain bounded" NFR and guardrail-2 alert lead-time.
MINOR:
  - Rollback's critical step "regenerate the projection with the Go tool" maps to no artifact in `contracts.files`/`contract_surface_future`; the regeneration capability has no named owner/registration (CL-001).
  - `design_pack.decisions` depends on BI-PF-1274 (cursor reads) but BI-PF-1274 is absent from `functional_spec.dependencies`/`design_pack.dependencies`, while traceability routes cursor tests to BI-PF-1268 — test/implementation item mismatch.
  - `contracts.files` lists `config/store-registry.json` without the "deferred" qualifier now applied in `dependencies` and `contract_surface_future`; Gate 1.5 evidence readers may assume registration exists at Gate 1.
NIT:
  - `risks` delta is byte-identical to context despite being in `changed_fields`, extending the scope noise already flagged for `spec_pack`/`functional_spec`.
  - Prior PENDING dispositions (design_pack.version → 2, deferred store-registry dependency, object-GC dry-run/bound) are satisfied by this delta; update the disposition ledger before Gate 1.5.
SUMMARY:
  - Verdict: AC-1/AC-2 met in delta; prior MAJORs verified ACTIONED (rollback freshness + regeneration source restored, frozen `contracts.files` repopulated).
  - Top risks: interim outbox backlog growth with explicitly inactive alerts between BI-PF-1268/1269; rollback's Go projection tool unnamed and unowned in the frozen contract surface.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=18576d8048a8
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Rollback depends on a "projection freshness bound of 5 minutes" to trigger degraded read-path state, yet neither `functional_spec.observability` nor `design_pack.observability` (both changed) defines a projection-age/freshness metric, alert, or detection owner — the rollback trigger is operationally undetectable.

NIT:

SUMMARY:

  - Top risks: rollback's freshness trigger has no corresponding observability row, ownership registration evidence is future-dated, and disposition ledger lag blocks a clean Gate 1.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

requirements: ADR accepted; design doc lists frozen contracts, migration matrix, and resolved open decisions.
language/ownership conflicts recorded (events.jsonl owner; event_bus facade).
invariants: PostgreSQL is the only event authority; events.jsonl is a read-only projection.
Each tenant has a monotonic seq; cursor reads use (tenant_id, seq).
A large payload is stored in object storage; the DB stores ref/sha256/size/content_type only.
Event insert and outbox insert commit in one transaction.
Only the Go event core writes events/outbox; no Python writer and no dual writer.
Bus transports carry notifications, never domain truth.
Ownership: core/events.py owns the read-only JSONL projection during migration; core/event_bus.py remains the compatibility facade; the Go event core owns PostgreSQL writes.
Any compatibility projection is generated from PostgreSQL and cannot be written as authority.

api: No runtime API change in this design item.
db: events(tenant_id, seq, event_id unique, occurred_at, type, version, correlation_id, causation_id, actor, payload jsonb, payload_ref, payload_sha256, size_bytes, content_type); append-only + RLS.
config: Payload inline threshold; event retention; outbox batch/retry limits. Values are deployment config, not code constants.

failure_matrix.expected: Fail closed; no file fallback and no partial event.

failure_matrix.case: Object store put fails for large payload
failure_matrix.expected: Fail closed before committing the event row.
Retry at-least-once; dedupe by event_id; move to DLQ after limit.
Reject unknown/future cursor with EVENT_CURSOR_INVALID; cursor=0 returns from start; never cross-tenant.

failure_matrix.case: Event DB commit fails after object put
failure_matrix.expected: Compensate/orphan-mark the object; GC only by explicit store tool; no event row visible.

failure_matrix.case: Retention deletes an object still referenced by a live event
failure_matrix.expected: Delete only when no live event row references the payload_ref; GC verifies reference count before object delete.
Feature flag stays off or cleanup+row-count alert bounds growth; no silent accumulation.

dependencies: ADR-0005 (Go event core, Python thin client)
deferred: config/store-registry.json registration lands with BI-PF-1268/1269
security: Server-resolved tenant context; PostgreSQL RLS on event and outbox reads/writes.
No provider URL as object identity; opaque refs + sha256.
Runtime roles are NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS; RLS applies to all event/outbox access.
Object references are tenant-scoped; provider URLs are never identity.
observability: Event append p95 < 100 ms; error rate >1% for 5 min pages.
Outbox lag p95 < 30 s; >5 min for 10 min pages.
Object payload store failures >0 for 5 min pages.
Outbox row count: >50k for 5 min pages; retention age >7 days pages; cleanup job failure pages.
Projection freshness: generated_at age >300 s for 5 min pages; owner platform-oncall; read path switches to degraded when stale.
performance: Indexed (tenant_id, seq); bounded inline payload threshold; paginated cursor reads; metadata-only event lists.
rollout: Design approval only in BI-PF-1266. Implementation starts at BI-PF-1267 contracts and BI-PF-1268 store/core.
design_pack.rollback: Stop the Go writer first. Keep the last generated JSONL projection read-only with a freshness bound of 5 minutes; if older, mark the read path degraded and do not rebuild from Python. Restore the event authority from PostgreSQL PITR/backup when DB returns, regenerate the projection with the Go tool, verify cursor/outbox parity, then resume. Never let Python write authority.
decisions: Transactional outbox; bus is optional transport.
Go event core; Python thin client.
Q1 packaging resolved: extend go/pfcore first; split only if measured.
Q2 run model resolved: library invocation for emit/read; dispatcher daemon later.
Q3 SSE resolved: API edge reads PostgreSQL cursors; no Go HTTP server in this phase.
Q4 writer resolved: Go event core is the sole PostgreSQL writer at cutover; JSONL is projection only.
Q5 Python handoff resolved: core/events.py calls the Go core; no dual writer.
API delta: none. Existing events route response shape is unchanged; BI-PF-1274 implements cursor reads behind it.
Outbox lag/DLQ thresholds are inactive until BI-PF-1269 dispatcher is deployed; rollout must enable alerting with that item.
BI-PF-1268 outbox writes stay feature-flagged off until BI-PF-1269 dispatcher; if enabled early, bound outbox rows (<100k), retention 7 days, alert at 50k/5 min, cleanup job required.
guardrails: No new Python under shipped roots.
CL-008: backup/restore = PostgreSQL PITR + object-store manifest; DB-down = fail closed with startup check; dry-run bounded to 1000 events; fail-able test = cursor/outbox parity test in BI-PF-1268.
Object GC/retention: dry-run first, delete bound 1000 objects per run, and delete only when reference count is zero.
Interim outbox bound/cleanup/alert is mandatory before enabling BI-PF-1268 outbox writes; no unbounded silent growth.
learnings: A durable cursor requires DB ordering, not timestamp comparison.
Payload size must be bounded independently of event count.

migration_matrix.compat: public API unchanged; JSONL projection read-only

design_pack.rollback_ref: Canonical rollback: functional_spec.rollback and design_pack.rollback are identical.
design_pack.ssot: docs/EVENTING-ALERTING-SSOT-DESIGN.md is design SSOT; engineering/design/BI-PF-1266.md and spec-pack are generated references.
contract_surface_future: go/pfcore/events.go owns projection regeneration from PostgreSQL backup/parity source.
design_pack.ownership_registration: Single-writer registration for the facade seam is evidenced by config/store-registry.json entries added in BI-PF-1268/BI-PF-1269; this design item does not mutate runtime stores.
design_pack.contract_surface_note: Frozen contract surface at Gate 1; implementation changes land in BI-PF-1267/1268/1269, not this design item.

outcome: PostgreSQL is the event authority with per-tenant seq/cursor; large payloads use object storage; outbox feeds transports.

requirements.title: Persist canonical events in PostgreSQL with tenant seq
requirements.preconditions: Tenant context and DB authority are available.
requirements.trigger: A producer emits a canonical event.
requirements.inputs: Envelope with event_id, type, payload, tenant.
requirements.outputs: Append-only event row with tenant seq.
acceptance: Given a valid tenant and event When it is emitted Then exactly one event row is appended with a monotonic seq.
requirements.verification: Design review plus BI-PF-1268 contract tests.

requirements.title: Store large event payloads as object references
requirements.preconditions: Payload exceeds the configured inline threshold.
requirements.outputs: Object ref, sha256, size and content type in the event row.
requirements.idempotency: Reference content is content-addressed by sha256.
requirements.data_rules: DB never stores bytes above threshold.
requirements.edge_cases: Object store unavailable or hash mismatch.
acceptance: Given an oversized payload When the event is emitted Then it is stored by reference and round-trips with sha256 verification.
requirements.verification: Design review plus BI-PF-1268 object-payload tests.

requirements.title: Dispatch through outbox with at-least-once dedupe
requirements.outputs: Delivered event; deduped by event_id; DLQ on exhaustion.
acceptance: Given a committed event When dispatch is retried Then the consumer receives it at least once and dedupes by event_id.
requirements.verification: Design review plus BI-PF-1269 dispatcher tests.
